<reflection>
After three experiments, M4 remains the best-fit model, but many mechanisms still have similar negative log-likelihoods, indicating insufficient discrimination. The third experiment introduced product (P=0.2) and altered the rankings slightly, but the top group (M4, M5, M12, M17, M16, etc.) remains clustered. So far, all experiments have used substrate concentration S=2.0 M. To further discriminate, we need to probe substrate dependence. Lowering substrate concentration will reveal whether the kinetics follow simple saturation (Michaelis-Menten) or show complexities like substrate inhibition, substrate-induced deactivation, or multiple substrate binding. This will differentiate mechanisms such as M7 (substrate binding to catalyst-substrate complex), M11 (substrate deactivation), M16 (substrate deactivation of catS), and others. The aim of the third experiment (product effect) was achieved, but we need to explore substrate variation to reduce uncertainty across the entire set.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
We propose an experiment with low substrate concentration (0.5 M) while keeping catalyst at 0.05 M and product at 0 M. This allows direct comparison with run1 (S=2.0, cat=0.05, P=0) to isolate substrate dependence. At low substrate, mechanisms that involve substrate inhibition or deactivation may behave differently relative to simple reversible mechanisms. For example, M7 includes S + catS <=> catS2; at low S, this step may be less significant, potentially making M7 less competitive. Similarly, mechanisms with substrate deactivation (M11, M16) might show reduced deactivation at low S, altering the progress curve shape. Mechanisms like M4 (which involves a different catalytic species X) may also exhibit distinct substrate dependence. This design avoids extreme conditions (substrate is still within the moderate range) and provides complementary information to previous runs, targeting substrate-sensitive mechanisms broadly. It is effective because it discriminates among many mechanisms simultaneously, not just a single pair, and avoids repeating similar regimes.
</hypothesis>
